prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Create a Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape aspect ratio about 3:2, crisp voxel style, vanilla Minecraft blocks only, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT a straight-on front elevation (orthographic), RIGHT a three-quarter front-right view at the same scale. Both views depict exactly the same build. Skilled human builder quality: real massing, depth with features proud of the wall and recessed openings, framed openings, real roof verges, eaves and ridge, sub-block detail using stairs, slabs, fences, walls, trapdoors and lanterns. Keep all shapes on a Minecraft block grid, including stepped arches and polygonal turret; no smooth real-world curves.
Site: A suburban McMansion seen from the cul-de-sac street, front facing the viewer. On the left, a wide three-car garage wing with three white carriage-style doors (small window panes along their tops), black-shuttered windows of a bonus room above, and a hipped dark asphalt-shingle roof with two dormers. Beyond it, in the middle, a two-storey beige-sided main block under a tall steep front gable in dark slate shingles. Below the gable, a double-height white portico with four tall quartz columns, a fanlighted double door with sidelights, and a big arched palladian window above it. Left of the portico, a small gabled dormer on the main roof. To the right, a hipped family wing whose front corner is a round-ish turret bay with a conical dark-slate cap and a thin finial, tall narrow arched windows, a big stone chimney on its back. The lower storey of the front is grey stone veneer (andesite, stone, cobblestone mix), with beige siding above, a white belt course between the storeys, white quoins at the corners, white window sills and hoods, and black shutters on the tall arched windows. A wide light-grey concrete driveway runs to the garage, with a stone-brick front walk to the portico, carriage lamp posts, a mailbox, a manicured lawn with rounded azalea shrubs and flower strips along the foundation, and a young oak with a stake on the right lawn. Behind, a spruce back deck with a railing, visible in the three-quarter view where possible.
Build dimensions: 44 blocks wide (x), 32 deep (z), 14 tall to the ridge/finial; 2 storeys plus attic. Show compact proportional massing consistent with this limit.
Use the following palette by exact Minecraft ids. Name the blocks with a compact readable palette legend beneath the views, grouped by role; prioritize accurate views over excessive lettering:
siding: birch_planks, birch_slab, birch_stairs.
veneer: andesite, stone, cobblestone, stone_bricks, stone_brick_stairs, stone_brick_slab, stone_brick_wall, andesite_stairs, andesite_slab, andesite_wall.
trim: quartz_block, smooth_quartz, smooth_quartz_stairs, smooth_quartz_slab, quartz_pillar, chiseled_quartz_block, quartz_stairs, quartz_slab.
roof: deepslate_tiles, deepslate_tile_stairs, deepslate_tile_slab, cobbled_deepslate, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, cobbled_deepslate_slab, blackstone, blackstone_stairs, blackstone_slab.
accents: black_concrete, dark_oak_trapdoor, dark_oak_door, dark_oak_planks, blackstone_wall, iron_bars, lantern, iron_chain, glass_pane, white_concrete, iron_trapdoor, cauldron, dark_oak_fence, oak_fence.
ground: grass_block, coarse_dirt, light_gray_concrete, gray_concrete, polished_andesite, smooth_stone, stone, stone_bricks, stone_brick_slab.
plants: azalea_leaves, flowering_azalea_leaves, oak_log, oak_leaves, short_grass, poppy, allium, peony, rose_bush, lilac, white_tulip.
deck: spruce_planks, spruce_log, spruce_fence, spruce_stairs, spruce_slab.
interior: oak_stairs, oak_planks.
Construct garage doors from white_concrete and iron_trapdoor with glass_pane top lights; shutters from dark_oak_trapdoor and black_concrete; entrance from paired dark_oak_door and glass_pane; lamps from lantern, iron_chain and blackstone_wall; mailbox from cauldron and iron_trapdoor on dark_oak_fence; tree stake from oak_fence. Use no blocks outside the named palette. No vehicles. Soft neutral lighting, clear pixelated vanilla material textures, uncluttered sheet with entire building and landscape visible in both views.
changes: Generated with the built-in image tool and saved unchanged as concept.png in the current directory.

Block assignments describe visual matches and construction equivalents; an image cannot establish exact block identities. The full planned palette is retained, including blocks shown only in the legend.
The image adds dark entrance planters containing small shrubs, interpreted as cauldron planters and potted_azalea; flower_pot and potted_azalea extend the planned palette.
Small circular ornamental details appear in the front gables. Their curved appearance has no exact vanilla block equivalent.
The arches, fanlights, window muntins, garage panels and column detailing include finer or smoother geometry than vanilla blocks can reproduce exactly.
The left elevation shows ground and roof surfaces, so it is not a strict straight-on orthographic elevation.
The two views do not maintain an exactly verifiable common scale or identical geometry; roof intersections, turret proportions and window spacing vary.
The dimension captions state 44 by 32 by 14 blocks, but the visible geometry does not establish those dimensions and appears too finely subdivided and tall for a literal 14-block height.
Four separate portico columns are not clearly distinguishable; the front view primarily shows two prominent columns.
The upper entrance window is a large arched opening rather than a clearly articulated three-part Palladian window.
Entrance sidelights are not clearly separated from the door surround.
The rear spruce deck appears as a two-level balcony and deck structure with tall supports, expanding the requested back deck.
The young oak has several surrounding stakes instead of a single stake, and additional trees appear at the site edges and rear.
The image adds a street, sidewalk, curb, clipped hedge borders, entrance planters and extra wall-mounted carriage lanterns.
The mailbox resembles a solid black rectangular box with a white cap rather than a clearly recognizable cauldron and iron-trapdoor assembly.
Some legend labels replace underscores with spaces or contain lettering errors; the JSON uses the supplied exact ids.
